title: Automated Quantification of Neuronal Cells Using Agilent BioTek Cytation System
author: Broeglin, Buetzberger, et al.

This section outlines the immunostaining for βIII-tubulin to visualize neurites for image-based outgrowth analysis. Negative controls are essential to validate immunostaining specificity and background levels; therefore, samples processed i) without primary antibody, ii) without secondary antibody, or iii) without any antibody should be included to assess non-specific binding and cellular autofluorescence. This section describes the image acquisition on the Agilent BioTek Cytation instrument and analysis procedure for neurite outgrowth quantification using the Gen5 software Neurite Outgrowth module. Similar results can be expected from additional Agilent BioTek automated imaging instrumentation. The parameters below are optimized for the cellular models used in this study and should be adjusted for each specific model.10.Capture a reference image with the DAPI and RFP channels.a.Open the Gen5 software.b.Click “Manual Mode”.c.Enter the parameters corresponding to your experimental conditions:i.Objective, Filter set, Microplate format, Vessel type.d.Select a reference well.e.Select the DAPI channel (nuclear channel, Excitation/Emission: 377/447 nm).f.Click “Find image”.Note: The Agilent BioTek automated cell imagers perform autofocus and autoexposure adjustments until a clear image is obtained.g.Adjust the image acquisition settings.i.Illumination: 10.ii.Integration time: 5.iii.Gain: 14.Note: Image acquisition settings may need to be adjusted between assays based on staining efficiency and sample properties.h.Identify the most representative field of your sample.i.Click “Capture”.Note: Image.j.Repeat the procedure for the RFP channel (neurite staining channel, Excitation/Emission: 531/593 nm).Image acquisition settings.i.Illumination: 10.ii.Integration time: 34.iii.Gain: 24.1.k.Click “Image Preprocessing”.Note: Image preprocessing is optional and performs background subtraction using a rolling-ball algorithm, a common processing method used in fluorescence microscopy to better visualize the cellular staining across a broad range of signal-to-noise ratios.l.Enter the rolling ball size for each channel:i.DAPI: 30 μm.ii.RFP: 100 μm.Note: The rolling ball size controls the background smoothing radius and is recommended to be greater than the maximum object size to be detected.Note: Exposure time and camera gain may need to be adjusted during reference image acquisition and preprocessing, depending on the neuronal marker used for immunostaining.11.Optimize neurite detection settings.a.Click “Neurite outgrowth analysis”.b.The default parameters provide a good starting point for most cell culture neurite outgrowth analysis. These parameters were further adjusted to optimize neurite and soma detection for this neuronal model (see Table 1).Table 1Settings for the neurite outgrowth analysis of the SH-SY5Y cellsNeurite Outgrowth Analysis settingsSoma detectionßIII-tubulin (RFP channel)Threshold Slider Level41Minimum/Maximum Size5/100 μmSoma Closing Size0 μmOptimized Soma Using Nuclear SignalCheckedRolling Ball Diameter50Nucleus Detection (DAPI Channel)Threshold Slider Level17Minimum/Maximum Size8/100 μmMinimum Nucleus/Soma Overlap15%Maximum Nucleus/Soma Distance20 μmNeuritesThreshold Slider Level−31Neurite Mask Closing Size1 μmRolling Ball Diameter5 μmOnly Keep Neurites Connected to a SomaCheckedDiscard Short Ending Branches10 μmNote: It is recommended to optimize nucleus and soma detection first, followed by neurite mask optimization.Note: These settings are optimized for SH-SY5Y cells and should be adjusted for other cell types, particularly nucleus/soma size and rolling ball diameter. Examples of settings for iPSC-derived and primary neuron culture models can be found on the related Application Note.812.Create the Gen5 experiment.a.Click “Create experiment from an image set” button in Gen5 software to import all the imaging and analysis settings (Part 4, Steps 1 and 2) into a new experiment for automated whole-plate imaging.Note: Image resolution is set to 1992 × 1992 pixels.b.Define the plate layout.c.Set the desired automated focus method.Note: The Laser autofocus option increases acquisition speed and focus reproducibility while reducing the risk of photobleaching.d.Images will be collected in the center of the well by default. To change the imaging location, use the “Beacons” feature to set fixed imaging regions of interest.Note: In this setup, five beacons were positioned in the central area and four at the periphery of each well to provide representative coverage of neurite outgrowth across the entire well. It is recommended to set at least 3–4 beacons per well. To apply the same beacon locations to all wells, select the corresponding option.e.Click “Run” to automatically collect images and perform neurite outgrowth image analysis.f.Neurite outgrowth analysis results are visualized in Gen5 software and can be exported for further evaluation.g.Generate summary figures and statistical analysis across datasets.Note: Figures and statistical analyses were performed using GraphPad Prism software.

steps.title: Prepare growth medium
steps.instruction: Prepare SH‑SY5Y culture medium by adding 10 % fetal bovine serum, 5 % horse serum, 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin, and 1 % GlutaMAX to high‑glucose DMEM, mix well and store at +4 °C (stable up to 1 month).

steps.title: Passage cells and plate new dishes
steps.instruction: Passage cells and plate fresh dishes for experiments and future culture.

substeps.instruction: Check confluency (~80 %) in 10 cm² dishes containing 10 mL growth medium.
Aspirate medium and wash once with 10 mL calcium‑magnesium‑free PBS (−) for 1 min.
Add 1.5 mL Accutase to cover the surface, then aspirate the Accutase.
Incubate the dish for ~5 min at 20 °C (lid closed) and verify detachment under a microscope.
Resuspend cells in 4–5 mL growth medium (volume depends on confluency).
Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL conical tube and add growth medium as needed.
Prepare two new 10 cm² dishes with 10 mL fresh growth medium each.
Distribute the recovered cells between the two dishes using a figure‑8 motion for homogeneous plating (one dish for experiments, one for future culture).

steps.title: Apply antibiotic selection
steps.instruction: Add selection antibiotics to maintain pressure on engineered lines.

substeps.instruction: Add blasticidin to the P301L dish to a final concentration of 4.5 µg/mL.
Add hygromycin to the APP dish to a final concentration of 300 µg/mL.

steps.title: Incubate cells
steps.instruction: Place all dishes in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: Wear gloves, safety glasses and work in a ventilated hood.
Heat 800 mL 1× PBS (−) to 60 °C.
Add 40 g paraformaldehyde powder while stirring on a hot plate with magnetic stirrer.
Add NaOH dropwise until the powder is fully dissolved.
Adjust the final volume to 1 L with 1× PBS (−).
Adjust pH to 6.9 using HCl solution.

steps.title: Filter and store formaldehyde
steps.instruction: Cool, filter and store the 4 % formaldehyde solution.

substeps.instruction: Cool the solution to room temperature.
Filter through a 0.2 µm mesh filter.
Store in a glass bottle at +4 °C (stable up to 1 month; aliquots may be frozen at −20 °C).

steps.title: Coat plates with laminin
steps.instruction: Coat black‑walled 96‑well clear‑bottom plates with laminin.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 10 µg/mL laminin solution in PBS (+) from a 0.5 mg/mL stock.
Add the laminin solution to each well of the plate.
Incubate the plate for 1 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Count and seed cells
steps.instruction: Count cells and seed them uniformly onto coated plates.

substeps.instruction: Detach cells as described in the passaging step.
Dilute cells 1:10 in Trypan Blue.
Count using a Neubauer hemocytometer (formula: (Cell1+Cell2)×Dilution×10⁴).
Dilute cells in growth medium to a final concentration of 5 000 cells per well (acceptable range 2 500–10 000 depending on line).
Seed 100 µL of cell suspension per well of the laminin‑coated plate, avoiding outer wells.
Add 200 µL 1× PBS (−) to each outer well to reduce evaporation.
Incubate the plate for 1 h at 20 °C to improve adherence.
Transfer the plate to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for continued culture.

steps.title: Fix cells with formaldehyde
steps.instruction: Fix cells using the prepared 4 % formaldehyde solution.

substeps.instruction: Warm the 4 % formaldehyde to 37 °C in a water bath.
Aspirate the differentiation medium from each well.
Add 50 µL per well of the pre‑warmed 4 % PFA solution.
Incubate 10 min at 20 °C.
Wash three times with 100 µL per well 1× PBS (−) for 1 min each (collect waste in a dedicated chemical waste container).

steps.title: Permeabilize and block wells
steps.instruction: Permeabilize cells and block nonspecific binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.15 % Triton X‑100 in 1× PBS (−).
Remove PBS from wells and add 50 µL per well of Triton solution.
Incubate 15 min at 20 °C.
Prepare 2 % BSA in PBS (−) (1 % = 10 mg/mL).
Wash wells three times with 100 µL PBS (−) for 1 min each.
Add 50 µL per well of 2 % BSA solution.
Incubate 1 h at 20 °C.
Dilute R&D MAB 1195 anti‑βIII‑tubulin (mouse) 1:1000 in 1 % BSA.
Aspirate the blocking buffer from each well.
Add 50 µL per well of the primary antibody solution.
Seal the plate with Parafilm to prevent evaporation.
Incubate overnight at +4 °C.

steps.title: Incubate secondary antibody and DAPI
steps.instruction: Apply secondary antibody and nuclear stain, then store.

substeps.instruction: Wash three times with 100 µL PBS (−) for 1 min each.
Dilute Abcam 175473 goat anti‑mouse Alexa 568 1:1000 in 1 % BSA.
Add 50 µL per well of the secondary antibody solution.
Incubate 1 h at 20 °C in the dark.
Wash three times with 100 µL PBS (−) for 1 min each.
Dilute DAPI 1:1000 in 1× PBS (−).
Add 50 µL per well of DAPI solution.
Incubate 5 min at 20 °C in the dark.
Wash three times with 100 µL PBS (−) for 1 min each.
Seal the plate with Parafilm.
Store at +4 °C protected from light (stable 2–4 weeks).

steps.title: Acquire reference images on Cytation
steps.instruction: Capture DAPI and RFP reference images using the Cytation instrument and Gen5 software.

substeps.instruction: Open Gen5, select Manual Mode and enter objective, filter set, plate format and vessel type.
Choose a reference well and select the DAPI channel (excitation/emission 377/447 nm).
Set illumination 10, integration time 5, gain 14 and click “Find image”.
Adjust autofocus/exposure as needed, then click “Capture”.
Repeat for the RFP channel (excitation/emission 531/593 nm) with illumination 10, integration time 34, gain 24.
Optionally run Image Preprocessing: select rolling‑ball background subtraction (30 µm for DAPI, 100 µm for RFP).

steps.title: Set neurite analysis parameters
steps.instruction: Configure neurite outgrowth detection settings in Gen5.

substeps.instruction: Open Neurite Outgrowth analysis.
Soma detection (βIII‑tubulin, RFP channel): threshold 41, size 5–100 µm, closing size 0 µm, use nuclear signal, rolling‑ball diameter 50 µm.
Nucleus detection (DAPI channel): threshold 17, size 8–100 µm, minimum overlap 15 %, max distance 20 µm.
Neurite detection: threshold –31, mask closing size 1 µm, rolling‑ball diameter 5 µm, keep neurites connected to soma, discard short endings <10 µm.
Optimize nucleus/soma detection first, then neurite mask.

steps.title: Create and run Gen5 experiment
steps.instruction: Set up a full‑plate automated acquisition and analysis in Gen5.

substeps.instruction: Click “Create experiment from an image set” and import all acquisition and analysis settings.
Set image resolution to 1992 × 1992 pixels.
Define the plate layout.
Select laser autofocus for rapid, reproducible focusing.
Configure beacons (e.g., five central and four peripheral per well; at least 3–4 beacons per well).
Click “Run” to collect images and perform neurite outgrowth analysis automatically.
Export analysis results and generate summary figures.
Perform statistical analysis (e.g., with GraphPad Prism).

description: This protocol focuses on assessing neurite outgrowth capacity in differentiated SH-SY5Y cells treated with brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), rotenone, or engineered to express Alzheimer’s disease-linked pathological proteins such as amyloid precursor protein (APP) and mutant tau (P301L). These treatments and cell models were selected to demonstrate the sensitivity and accuracy of the Agilent BioTek Gen5 software Neurite Outgrowth module in detecting subtle alterations in neurite outgrowth parameters induced by pharmacological or genetic perturbations. The native human neuroblastoma cell line SH-SY5Y comes from ATCC (CRL-2266). The P301L cells are SH-SY5Y cells stably overexpressing the P301Ltau mutation in the microtubule-associated protein Tau (MAPT) gene. Cells were kindly provided by Prof. Jürgen Götz Laboratory (Queensland Brain Institute, University of Queensland, Brisbane, Australia), which generated the cell line using lentiviral gene transfer.1 Cell clones stably expressing the full-length human hTau40 bearing the P301L mutation and a green fluorescent protein (GFP) tag were selected by adding 4.5 μg/mL of blasticidin to the culture medium. We previously showed that these cells exhibit abnormal tau hyperphosphorylation and mitochondrial impairments.2,3 The APP cells are SH-SY5Y cells stably overexpressing the entire coding region of human wild-type APP (APP695). The cell line was generated using Lipofectamine Plus mixture.4 Cell clones stably expressing APP were maintained in medium containing 300 μg/mL hygromycin to ensure stable vector expression. We previously showed that APP cells secrete Amyloid-β1-40 at levels in the pg/mL range and exhibit mitochondrial impairments.5 All the steps described below are performed under sterile conditions until the culture fixation step.
